key_distinction.foreign_currency_transaction: Single transaction denominated in foreign currency → Recognize gain/loss in NET INCOME
key_distinction.foreign_currency_translation: Translating entire foreign subsidiary's financial statements → Translation adjustment goes to OCI (Other Comprehensive Income)

functional_currency.definition: Primary currency of entity's economic environment where it generates and expends cash
determination_factors: Cash flows: Currency that mainly affects sales prices and costs
Sales market: Currency of country where products are sold
Expenses: Currency in which labor, materials, other costs are paid
Financing: Currency in which funds are generated
Intercompany transactions: High volume suggests parent's currency as functional

three_scenarios.usd_is_functional: Use TEMPORAL METHOD (also called REMEASUREMENT method)
three_scenarios.highly_inflationary_economy: If inflation >100% cumulative over 3 years, use USD as functional currency → TEMPORAL METHOD

current_rate_method.when_used: Foreign currency is functional currency (subsidiary operates independently)

balance_sheet_translation.assets_and_liabilities: ALL translated at CURRENT rate (rate at balance sheet date)
balance_sheet_translation.stockholders_equity: Translated at HISTORICAL rates (rates when transactions occurred)
balance_sheet_translation.exception: Retained earnings calculated as: Beginning RE + NI - Dividends

income_statement_translation.revenues_and_expenses: Translated at AVERAGE rate for period
income_statement_translation.practical: Use weighted average rate for year

current_rate_method.translation_adjustment: Goes to OTHER COMPREHENSIVE INCOME (OCI), accumulated in stockholders' equity
current_rate_method.mnemonic: CASE: Current rate for Assets and liabilities, equity at hiStorical, income at avErage

temporal_method.when_used: USD is functional currency (subsidiary is extension of parent operations) OR highly inflationary economy

balance_sheet_translation.monetary_items: Translated at CURRENT rate (cash, receivables, payables, long-term debt)

nonmonetary_items.historical_cost: Translated at HISTORICAL rate (inventory at cost, PPE, intangibles)
nonmonetary_items.fair_value: Translated at rate when FV determined

income_statement_translation.exceptions: Items related to nonmonetary assets/liabilities use HISTORICAL rates (COGS, depreciation, amortization)

temporal_method.mnemonic: MUST: Monetary at cUrrent, nonmonetary at hiStorical, gain/loss in neT income

temporal_method.assets_liabilities: Monetary at current, nonmonetary at historical

calculation_example_current_rate.facts: Foreign subsidiary with functional currency = local currency. Balance sheet: Cash 100K local currency (LC), Inventory 200K LC, PPE 500K LC, Payables 150K LC, Common stock 400K LC, RE 250K LC. Current rate $1 = 10 LC. Historical rate for equity $1 = 8 LC. Average rate $1 = 9 LC.
calculation_example_current_rate.translation_adjustment_goes_to: OCI (part of accumulated OCI in equity)

calculation_example_temporal.facts: Foreign subsidiary with functional currency = USD. Balance sheet: Cash 100K LC, Inventory (at cost) 200K LC, PPE 500K LC. Payables 150K LC. Common stock 400K LC, RE 250K LC. Current rate $1 = 10 LC. Historical rate for inventory $1 = 9 LC, PPE $1 = 8 LC, equity $1 = 8 LC.

remeasurement_balance_sheet.remeasurement_gain_loss: Plug to balance (goes to net income)

highly_inflationary_economy.treatment: Use USD as functional currency regardless of economic indicators → Apply TEMPORAL method
highly_inflationary_economy.reason: Local currency too unstable to be meaningful functional currency

foreign_currency_transactions.definition: Single transaction (sale, purchase, loan) denominated in foreign currency

two_date_approach.transaction_date: Record at spot rate on transaction date
two_date_approach.balance_sheet_date: Revalue monetary items (receivables, payables) at current rate. Recognize gain/loss in net income.
two_date_approach.settlement_date: Record final gain/loss based on rate at settlement

foreign_currency_transactions.example: Dec 1: Purchase inventory for 100K euros when $1 = 1 euro. Record at $100K. Dec 31 (BS date): $1 = 0.9 euros (euro strengthened). Payable now $111K (100K / 0.9). Recognize loss $11K in net income. Jan 15 (settlement): Pay when $1 = 0.95 euros. Payment $105K (100K / 0.95). Recognize gain $6K in net income.

forward_exchange_contracts.hedging_purpose: Lock in exchange rate to eliminate uncertainty
forward_exchange_contracts.accounting: If qualifies as hedge: Apply hedge accounting (defer gains/losses). If not hedge: Mark to market through net income.

cpa_exam_tips: Transaction gains/losses → NET INCOME. Translation adjustments → OCI.
Current rate method: ALL assets/liabilities at current rate. Gain/loss to OCI.
Temporal method: Monetary at current, nonmonetary at historical. Gain/loss to NI.
COGS/Depreciation: Current rate method uses average rate. Temporal method uses historical rate.
Highly inflationary (>100% over 3 years) → Use temporal method
Functional currency determination is KEY to knowing which method to use

method_selection: 1. Determine functional currency (foreign currency or USD?)
2. If foreign currency is functional → Current rate method → Translation adjustment to OCI
3. If USD is functional (or highly inflationary) → Temporal method → Remeasurement gain/loss to NI
translation_steps_current_rate: 1. Translate ALL assets and liabilities at current rate
3. Plug translation adjustment to balance (goes to OCI)
translation_steps_temporal: 1. Translate monetary items at current rate
2. Translate nonmonetary items at historical rate
4. Plug remeasurement gain/loss to balance (goes to NI)
common_mistakes: Confusing transaction gains/losses (NI) with translation adjustments (OCI)
Using current rate for all items under temporal method (should be monetary only)
Using historical rate for revenues under current rate method (should be average)
Forgetting highly inflationary economy rule (>100% over 3 years → temporal method)

key_points: Transaction gains/losses → Net Income. Translation adjustments → OCI.
Current rate method: Foreign currency is functional. ALL assets/liabilities at current rate. Translation adjustment to OCI.
Temporal method: USD is functional. Monetary at current, nonmonetary at historical. Remeasurement gain/loss to NI.
Highly inflationary economy (>100% over 3 years) → Use temporal method
COGS/Depreciation: Current rate method = average rate. Temporal method = historical rate.
Functional currency determination drives method selection
